tags.name: PREC
tags.default: Normal

summary.beginner: Picks how fine the calculation grids are. Use Accurate for anything that needs forces or stress.
summary.intermediate: FFT grid density and default cutoff
summary.pro: Normal: standard for relaxations and MD; small wrap-around errors are possible. Accurate: denser grids that avoid wrap-around errors. Recommended for production forces, stress, phonons. High: legacy; like Accurate with ENCUT = 1.3 × ENMAX. Prefer Accurate plus an explicit ENCUT. Low: coarse grids for rough pre-relaxation of large systems. Single (VASP 6): like Accurate, but the augmentation grid equals the coarse grid (one grid instead of two), saving memory.

tags.why: Accurate avoids wrap-around errors; needed for forces, stress, phonons, elastic.
tags.breaks: Normal can give wrap-around errors and noisy forces or stress.

corrections.now: "Single" refers to using a single FFT grid (the fine augmentation grid equals the coarse grid), not single-precision arithmetic.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ENCUT
tags.default: largest ENMAX in POTCAR

summary.beginner: The size of the plane-wave basis, set as an energy in eV. Bigger is more accurate and slower.
summary.pro: Higher ENCUT means more plane waves, a more complete basis, more memory and CPU time. If ENCUT is too low, stress and pressure suffer from Pulay stress: the basis set is not converged with respect to volume changes. Default: largest ENMAX of the POTCAR datasets (PREC = Normal/Accurate); PREC = High sets 1.3 × ENMAX.

tags.why: Stress converges much more slowly than energy, so cell relaxations and elastic runs need the 30% margin to suppress Pulay stress. Keep it identical in every calculation you compare.
tags.breaks: Too low gives wrong stress and lattice constants. Changing it between runs you compare makes the energies incomparable.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: EDIFF
tags.typical: 1E-5 relax; 1E-6 SCF/DOS; 1E-7–1E-8 elastic, phonons, optics, ε

summary.beginner: How tightly each electronic loop must converge. Smaller means more accurate forces and response properties.
summary.intermediate: SCF stop: energy change between electronic steps (eV)
summary.pro: The SCF loop stops when both the total free energy and the band-structure energy change by less than EDIFF between steps. EDIFF is a total-energy criterion, not per atom, so large cells effectively need a tighter value. Too loose → noisy forces and stress, which confuse the ionic optimizer. If a relaxation won't converge, tighten EDIFF first. EDIFF = 0 makes VASP always run exactly NELM steps.

tags.why: Forces and response properties come from derivatives of the wavefunction, so they need a far tighter SCF than the total energy does. Loose values give noisy forces and imaginary phonon modes.
tags.breaks: Too loose gives noisy forces and false imaginary phonon modes.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: EDIFFG
tags.default: EDIFF × 10

summary.beginner: When to stop a relaxation. A negative number means: stop when every force is smaller than that many eV per angstrom.
summary.intermediate: Ionic stop. >0: energy change (eV). <0: max force (eV/Å)
summary.pro: Positive: stop when the total-energy change between ionic steps is below EDIFFG (eV). Negative: stop when the force on every atom is below |EDIFFG| (eV/Å). More reliable for finding the true minimum. The force criterion ignores stress. In ISIF = 3 runs, check the stress (OUTCAR "in kB") separately. A tight EDIFFG needs a tight EDIFF (e.g. −0.005 with 1E-7); otherwise noisy forces keep the ions "chattering" around the minimum.

tags.why: Negative (force) criteria are more reliable. EDIFF should be at least 10× smaller than any energy-based EDIFFG.
tags.breaks: A positive value stops on energy change, which can end a relaxation too early. EDIFF should be at least 10 times smaller than any energy-based EDIFFG.

corrections.now: −0.001 is typical before phonon calculations. NEB runs normally use −0.01 to −0.05; −0.001 is rarely reachable on a band of images.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NELM
tags.default: NELM = 60, NELMIN = 2

summary.beginner: The most electronic steps allowed for each ionic step.
summary.intermediate: Max electronic steps per ionic step
summary.pro: NELM: hard limit on electronic steps. Reaching it means the step is unconverged, but VASP proceeds to the next ionic step anyway. NELMIN: forces at least this many steps, so the loop cannot stop "by accident" after the ions move. 4–8 is recommended for relaxations and MD; 8 or more for difficult systems and hybrids. If forces in OUTCAR look noisy or inconsistent between steps, raising NELMIN (and tightening EDIFF) helps.

tags.why: If a step hits NELM the forces are unconverged; fix mixing first rather than just raising NELM.
tags.breaks: If a step reaches NELM, the forces are not converged. Fix the mixing first rather than only raising NELM.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NELMIN
tags.default: NELM = 60, NELMIN = 2

summary.beginner: The fewest electronic steps allowed for each ionic step.
summary.intermediate: Min electronic steps per ionic step
summary.pro: NELM: hard limit on electronic steps. Reaching it means the step is unconverged, but VASP proceeds to the next ionic step anyway. NELMIN: forces at least this many steps, so the loop cannot stop "by accident" after the ions move. 4–8 is recommended for relaxations and MD; 8 or more for difficult systems and hybrids. If forces in OUTCAR look noisy or inconsistent between steps, raising NELMIN (and tightening EDIFF) helps.

tags.why: Prevents a too-early exit that yields poor forces.
tags.breaks: Too small can end the electronic loop too early and give poor forces.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NELMDL
tags.default: -5 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: How many start-up steps let the random starting wavefunctions settle before the density is updated. The value is negative: -5 by default, -12 for difficult starts.
summary.pro: Lets random wavefunctions settle before the density is updated.

tags.why: Lets random wavefunctions settle before the density is updated.
tags.breaks: A bad start can make the first steps wander; the handbook uses a more negative value for difficult starts.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ALGO
tags.default: Normal

summary.beginner: Chooses the method used to find the electron states. Normal is the safe choice; All or Damped help hard cases.
summary.pro: Normal: blocked Davidson. Robust. Fast: Davidson for the first steps, then RMM-DIIS. Faster; good default for most bulk work. VeryFast: RMM-DIIS only. Fast but fragile. All (Conjugate): all bands updated together. Robust for difficult metals, magnetic systems and hybrids. Damped: damped MD of the wavefunctions; recommended for hybrid functionals and hard cases.

tags.why: Normal is robust; Fast is quicker for simple systems; All/Damped for magnetic, +U, hybrids, meta-GGA, and stubborn SCF.
tags.breaks: The wrong choice can stall or oscillate in magnetic, +U, hybrid and meta-GGA runs.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ISMEAR
tags.default: ISMEAR = 1, SIGMA = 0.2

summary.beginner: How electrons are spread over energy levels near the Fermi level. 0 with a small SIGMA is the safe default for this handbook.
summary.pro: −5, tetrahedron with Blöchl corrections: accurate total energies and DOS for bulk. Needs at least 4 k-points. Do not use for relaxations of metals (forces are inaccurate). SIGMA is not used for the occupations. 0, Gaussian: safe for any system and for few k-points. Use SIGMA ≈ 0.03–0.05 for semiconductors and insulators; quote E0 (σ → 0). 1 or 2, Methfessel–Paxton: good for metals, SIGMA ≈ 0.1–0.2. −1, Fermi–Dirac: physical electronic temperature (finite-temperature DFT). Check the entropy term T·S in OUTCAR: divided by the number of atoms it should stay below about 1 meV/atom. If larger, ...

tags.why: 0 is safe everywhere. 1 for metal relaxations, never for semiconductors. −5 for accurate DOS and total energies on a uniform mesh with ≥ 4 k-points; not for band paths, not for metal forces.
tags.breaks: Method 1 on a semiconductor gives wrong energies. Method -5 should not be used for band paths or metal forces.

corrections.was: If ISMEAR = 0, 1 or 2 is used, SIGMA must also be set.
corrections.now: SIGMA has a default (0.2 eV), but that default suits metals only. Set it explicitly every time.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: SIGMA
tags.default: ISMEAR = 1, SIGMA = 0.2

summary.beginner: The width of that spreading, in eV. Small for insulators, larger for metals.
summary.pro: −5, tetrahedron with Blöchl corrections: accurate total energies and DOS for bulk. Needs at least 4 k-points. Do not use for relaxations of metals (forces are inaccurate). SIGMA is not used for the occupations. 0, Gaussian: safe for any system and for few k-points. Use SIGMA ≈ 0.03–0.05 for semiconductors and insulators; quote E0 (σ → 0). 1 or 2, Methfessel–Paxton: good for metals, SIGMA ≈ 0.1–0.2. −1, Fermi–Dirac: physical electronic temperature (finite-temperature DFT). Check the entropy term T·S in OUTCAR: divided by the number of atoms it should stay below about 1 meV/atom. If larger, ...

tags.why: Check grep EENTRO OUTCAR: the entropy term T·S should be below ~1 meV/atom.
tags.breaks: Too wide blurs gaps and adds an entropy error; check the T*S term in OUTCAR is below about 1 meV per atom.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ISPIN
tags.typical: 2 for any open-shell d/f system or radical

summary.beginner: Turns spin polarization on (2) or off (1). Use 2 for magnetic materials and open-shell atoms.
summary.pro: 1: non-spin-polarized; each orbital holds two electrons. Faster, half the memory. Fine for non-magnetic materials (Si, water). 2: separate spin-up and spin-down wavefunctions. Needed for ferromagnets (Fe, Co, Ni), antiferromagnets, radicals, many defects and surfaces. With ISPIN = 2, CHGCAR, DOSCAR and EIGENVAL hold two spin channels; OSZICAR reports the total moment (mag), and OUTCAR the site moments (LORBIT ≥ 10). CPU time and memory roughly double.

tags.why: A spin-polarized run started with no initial moment can stay non-magnetic; MAGMOM supplies the seed.
tags.breaks: A spin-polarized run with no starting moment can stay non-magnetic.

corrections.was: If ISPIN = 2 is set, MAGMOM must also be set.
corrections.now: MAGMOM is not mandatory: it defaults to 1.0 μB on every atom (ferromagnetic). Set it explicitly for antiferromagnets, strongly magnetic ions or any specific ordering.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: MAGMOM
tags.default: NIONS*1.0 (ISPIN = 2)

summary.beginner: The starting magnetic moment of each atom, in the same order as the POSCAR. Write 4*3.0 for four atoms at 3.0.
summary.intermediate: Initial moment per atom (μB), POSCAR order
summary.pro: One value per atom, in POSCAR order. Final moments (OSZICAR, OUTCAR) usually differ from the input; VASP relaxes them. Start slightly above the expected moment, e.g. Fe ≈ 3, Co ≈ 2, Ni ≈ 1, high-spin Mn²⁺/Fe³⁺ ≈ 5. VASP includes MAGMOM in its symmetry analysis, so an AFM pattern automatically lowers the symmetry.

tags.why: Start above the expected moment (3–5 for 3d ions). Count must equal NIONS (3×NIONS for non-collinear).
tags.breaks: The count must equal the number of atoms; a wrong count or order starts the wrong magnetic state.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NUPDOWN
tags.default: Not stated in the handbooks. See the VASP wiki page for NUPDOWN.

summary.beginner: Forces the difference between spin-up and spin-down electrons to a fixed number.
summary.pro: Forces a spin state for comparison; remove it for the final ground state.

tags.why: Forces a spin state for comparison; remove it for the final ground state.
tags.breaks: Left on by mistake it holds the system in a spin state that is not the ground state.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: LORBIT
tags.default: not set (no projections)

summary.beginner: Asks VASP to also write the density of states split by atom and orbital. Use 11.
summary.pro: 10: projections onto s, p, d (f) per atom. 11: as 10, further resolved into px, py, pz, dxy… The usual choice. 12: as 11, plus complex phase factors in PROCAR. For 10–12 the sphere radii come from the POTCAR (RWIGS there); for LORBIT = 0–2 RWIGS must be set in INCAR. Also prints site-resolved charges and magnetic moments (s, p, d) in OUTCAR.

tags.why: 11 writes lm-decomposed PDOS and PROCAR and site magnetic moments without needing RWIGS.
tags.breaks: Without it there is no projected DOS or PROCAR for plots by atom or orbital.

corrections.now: Phase factors come only with LORBIT = 12.

corrections.was: LORBIT = 12 uses a different projection grid for symmetry-based analysis.
corrections.now: LORBIT = 12 uses the same projections as 11 and adds the phase factors to PROCAR.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NEDOS

summary.beginner: The number of energy points in the density of states. More points give a smoother curve.
summary.intermediate: Points on the DOS energy grid
summary.pro: NEDOS: number of energy points. The default 301 is far too coarse for publication plots. EMIN, EMAX: absolute energy window (eV). Choose it around the Fermi level of the SCF run.

tags.why: Default 301 is too coarse for clean PDOS and optical spectra.
tags.breaks: The default is too coarse for clean projected DOS and optical spectra.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: EMIN
tags.default: NEDOS = 301

summary.beginner: The lowest energy of the DOS window, in eV on VASP absolute scale.
summary.pro: NEDOS: number of energy points. The default 301 is far too coarse for publication plots. EMIN, EMAX: absolute energy window (eV). Choose it around the Fermi level of the SCF run.

tags.why: Concentrates NEDOS points where you plot.
tags.breaks: A window that misses the Fermi level wastes points where you do not plot.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: EMAX
tags.default: NEDOS = 301

summary.beginner: The highest energy of the DOS window, in eV on VASP absolute scale.
summary.pro: NEDOS: number of energy points. The default 301 is far too coarse for publication plots. EMIN, EMAX: absolute energy window (eV). Choose it around the Fermi level of the SCF run.

tags.why: Concentrates NEDOS points where you plot.
tags.breaks: A window that misses the Fermi level wastes points where you do not plot.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ISTART
tags.default: 1 if WAVECAR exists, else 0

summary.beginner: Whether to start from random wavefunctions (0) or read the saved WAVECAR (1).
summary.pro: 0: new start, random wavefunctions. Use it when WAVECAR is corrupted or belongs to a different system. 1: continuation, read WAVECAR. The plane-wave basis is regenerated for the current cell at constant ENCUT. Use it after timeouts, when moving from coarse to accurate settings, or to start hard magnetic and metallic systems from a converged state. 2: continuation with a constant basis set (same plane waves as before). The effective cutoff changes with the cell. Used for energy-volume curves without Pulay-stress contamination. 3: full restart including wavefunction and charge-density ...

tags.why: See restart logic.
tags.breaks: Reading a corrupted or mismatched WAVECAR stops the run at start-up.

corrections.was: ISTART = 2: same as 1 but adjusts the basis set to a changed cell after ISIF = 3.
corrections.now: It is the reverse: ISTART = 1 rebuilds the basis for the new cell at constant cutoff. ISTART = 2 keeps the old basis set fixed.
ISTART = 3 is a full restart for MD that also reuses the wavefunction and charge prediction from TMPCAR.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ICHARG
tags.default: 2 if ISTART = 0, else 0

summary.beginner: Where the starting electron density comes from. 2 builds it from atoms, 1 reads CHGCAR, 11 reads CHGCAR and keeps it fixed.
summary.pro: 0: from the initial wavefunctions (WAVECAR). 1: read CHGCAR and continue self-consistency. 2: superposition of atomic charge densities (the usual fresh start). +10 (11, 12): the density is kept fixed (non-self-consistent). 11 reads CHGCAR: the standard setting for band structures and DOS.

tags.why: 11 for band structures and dense-mesh DOS.
tags.breaks: 11 needs a CHGCAR from the same structure, ENCUT, POTCAR and spin setting, and does not work with hybrids.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: IBRION
tags.default: −1 if NSW ≤ 1, else 0 (MD!)
tags.typical: 2 CG (relax); 6 elastic; not written for SCF (default −1 when NSW = 0)

summary.beginner: Chooses what VASP does with the ions: nothing, relax them, or displace them to get force constants.
summary.pro: −1: no ionic movement (static). 0: ab initio MD. Set POTIM (time step) and NSW; choose a thermostat with MDALGO and TEBEG/TEEND. 1: RMM-DIIS quasi-Newton. Efficient close to the minimum, can be unstable when forces are large. 2: conjugate gradient. Robust standard for starting relaxations from rough structures. 3: damped MD. Useful for poor starting geometries and NEB. 5 / 6: finite-difference force constants (phonons, Γ-point frequencies). 5 displaces every atom in every direction; 6 uses symmetry to reduce displacements and, with ISIF ≥ 3, also gives elastic constants. 7 / 8: the same via ...

tags.why: 2 far from minimum, 1 close to it. 6 + ISIF≥3 gives elastic constants. 8 gives force constants, ε and Z* by DFPT.
tags.breaks: Left unset with NSW above 1 it defaults to molecular dynamics. Always set it explicitly for relaxations.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ISIF
tags.default: 2 (relax), 0 (MD)
tags.typical: 2 ions; 3 ions+shape+volume; 4 ions+shape at fixed V

summary.beginner: Chooses what may change in a relaxation: only ions (2), ions and the whole cell (3), or ions and cell shape at fixed volume (4).
summary.intermediate: What relaxes and whether stress is computed
summary.pro: Needs IBRION > 0 and NSW > 0 to move anything. Slabs and surfaces: ISIF = 2. ISIF = 3 would shrink the vacuum. ISIF = 3 keeps the initial space group (a cubic cell stays cubic) unless the symmetry is broken in the input.

tags.why: 3 for equilibrium structures, 4 for E–V points, 2 for slabs and defects. ISIF=3 required with IBRION=6 for Cij.
tags.breaks: ISIF = 3 on a slab changes the vacuum. ISIF = 3 is required with IBRION = 6 for elastic constants.

corrections.was: ISIF = 7 is used for fitting an equation of state.
corrections.now: An equation of state is usually fitted from a series of fixed-volume calculations (ISIF = 4, or ISIF = 2 for cubic cells at scaled volumes). ISIF = 7 relaxes the volume isotropically.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NSW

summary.beginner: The most ionic steps allowed. 0 means a single calculation with no ion movement.
summary.pro: 0: one ionic step, no movement. Static energies, DOS, bands. Relaxation (IBRION = 1, 2, 3): upper limit on steps. If reached before EDIFFG is met, copy CONTCAR to POSCAR and restart. MD (IBRION = 0): exactly the number of time steps.

tags.why: Reaching NSW is not convergence; check for “reached required accuracy”.
tags.breaks: Reaching NSW is not convergence. Check the output for the message that the required accuracy was reached.

corrections.was: VASP exits immediately if NSW is not given for an MD run.
corrections.now: With the default NSW = 0, IBRION = 0 simply performs no MD steps. Always set NSW for MD.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: POTIM
tags.default: 0.5 (IBRION 1–3); none for MD

summary.beginner: The step size for moving ions, or the displacement size for finite differences, in angstrom.
summary.pro: MD: the time step in fs. About 0.5 fs with hydrogen, 1–2 fs for heavier atoms. Check the drift of E in OSZICAR. IBRION = 1, 2, 3: scales the trial step. Reduce it (e.g. 0.1) when a relaxation oscillates. IBRION = 5, 6: the displacement amplitude (default 0.015 Å).

tags.why: Lower it when relaxations oscillate or ZBRENT errors appear.
tags.breaks: Too large makes relaxations oscillate or fail with ZBRENT errors.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NFREE
tags.default: Not stated in the handbooks. See the VASP wiki page for NFREE.

summary.beginner: How many displacements per direction in finite-difference runs. 4 is more accurate and costs twice as much as 2.
summary.pro: 4 is more accurate (cancels anharmonic error), twice the cost.

tags.why: 4 is more accurate (cancels anharmonic error), twice the cost.
tags.breaks: Too few displacements leave more anharmonic error in force constants and elastic constants.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: LREAL
tags.default: .FALSE.

summary.beginner: Chooses whether some projections are done in real space (faster) or reciprocal space (more exact).
summary.intermediate: Projection in real or reciprocal space
summary.pro: .FALSE.: reciprocal space. Most accurate; cost grows faster with system size. Preferred for small cells, phonons, linear response and exact exchange. Auto: real space with automatically optimized projectors. Recommended for cells above roughly 20 atoms. On: real space with optimized projectors, precision set manually through ROPT. .TRUE.: real space with non-optimized projectors (legacy).

tags.why: Real-space projection introduces small force/energy errors; use .FALSE. for phonons, elastic, final energies.
tags.breaks: Real-space projection adds small errors; use .FALSE. for phonons, elastic constants and final energies.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: ADDGRID
tags.default: .FALSE.

summary.beginner: Adds an extra fine grid for some charges. It lowers noise in forces at little cost.
summary.intermediate: Extra fine grid for augmentation charges
summary.pro: .TRUE.: augmentation charges are evaluated on a grid twice as dense in each direction. This can reduce noise in forces and the egg-box effect (energy varying as an atom moves relative to the grid). With PREC = Accurate the gain is usually small. It is most often used for finite-difference phonons and very tight force criteria.

tags.why: Reduces force noise; marginal cost.
tags.breaks: Without it, phonon force constants can be noisier.

corrections.was: It is particularly helpful for HSE06 calculations to stabilize electronic convergence.
corrections.now: ADDGRID has no established role in hybrid-functional SCF convergence. For difficult HSE runs, adjust ALGO (Damped/All) and start from a converged PBE WAVECAR.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: LASPH
tags.default: Not stated in the handbooks. See the VASP wiki page for LASPH.

summary.beginner: Includes small non-spherical effects inside the atoms. Turn it on for d and f elements.
summary.pro: Required for meta-GGA; recommended for d/f elements, +U and hybrids.

tags.why: Required for meta-GGA; recommended for d/f elements, +U and hybrids.
tags.breaks: Missing it for +U, hybrids or d/f elements gives less accurate results; meta-GGA runs require it.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: LMAXMIX
tags.default: 2 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: How much detail about d and f electrons is kept when mixing densities. Use 4 for d elements, 6 for f.
summary.intermediate: Max l of one-centre densities kept in mixer/CHGCAR
summary.pro: Default 2 loses d/f occupation information; vital for +U and for ICHARG=11 runs on d/f systems.

tags.why: Default 2 loses d/f occupation information; vital for +U and for ICHARG=11 runs on d/f systems.
tags.breaks: The low default loses d/f occupation information, which matters for +U and for ICHARG = 11 runs.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: AMIX
tags.default: 0.4 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: How strongly new density is mixed in each step. Lower values calm unstable runs.
summary.pro: Lower AMIX damps charge sloshing in metals, slabs and magnets.

tags.why: Lower AMIX damps charge sloshing in metals, slabs and magnets.
tags.breaks: Too high can cause charge sloshing in metals, slabs and magnets.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: BMIX
tags.default: 1.0 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: A second mixing parameter that works with AMIX.
summary.pro: Lower AMIX damps charge sloshing in metals, slabs and magnets.

tags.why: Lower AMIX damps charge sloshing in metals, slabs and magnets.
tags.breaks: Poor values slow or stall the SCF loop.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: AMIX_MAG
tags.default: 1.6 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: The same as AMIX, but for the magnetization density.
summary.pro: Pair with low AMIX/BMIX for oscillating moments.

tags.why: Pair with low AMIX/BMIX for oscillating moments.
tags.breaks: Wrong values can make magnetic moments oscillate between steps.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: BMIX_MAG
tags.default: 1.0 (as stated in the Workflow Handbook dictionary)

summary.beginner: The same as BMIX, but for the magnetization density.
summary.pro: Pair with low AMIX/BMIX for oscillating moments.

tags.why: Pair with low AMIX/BMIX for oscillating moments.
tags.breaks: Wrong values can make magnetic moments oscillate between steps.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NBANDS
tags.default: Not stated in the handbooks. See the VASP wiki page for NBANDS.
tags.typical: default; 2–3× for optics; extra for band plots

summary.beginner: How many electron states (bands) are calculated, including empty ones.
summary.pro: Optics needs empty bands for transitions; must exceed occupied bands.

tags.why: Optics needs empty bands for transitions; must exceed occupied bands.
tags.breaks: Optics gives poor results without extra empty bands. It must exceed the number of occupied bands.
tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: NCORE

summary.beginner: How many cores work together on one band. It tunes speed only.
summary.pro: NCORE and the older NPAR describe the same split (NPAR = ranks / NCORE). NCORE is easier because it does not depend on the total number of ranks. Typical good values lie between 4 and the number of cores per socket; on a 32-core node try 4, 8 and 16 and time a few electronic steps. Reduces communication between nodes; most valuable for large supercells with few k-points.

tags.why: Comment out for IBRION = 6 (elastic), IBRION 7/8, LEPSILON, LELF.
tags.breaks: Must be commented out for IBRION = 6, IBRION 7/8, LEPSILON and LELF runs, or the run can fail.

corrections.was: NCORE was added to replace NPAR and is more efficient because it scales better.
corrections.now: Both tags still exist and set the same parallel layout. NCORE is simply more convenient to set; neither is more efficient for the same layout.

corrections.was: Setting NCORE equal to cores per node (e.g. 32) is the sweet spot.
corrections.now: The optimum is usually smaller (cores per socket or less). Benchmark rather than assume.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: KPAR

summary.beginner: Splits the k-points into groups that run side by side. It tunes speed only.
summary.pro: KPAR = 1: all MPI ranks work on each k-point in turn. KPAR > 1: ranks split into KPAR groups, each handling its own subset of k-points at the same time. Little communication between groups, so speed-up is often close to linear. Memory grows with KPAR, since each group holds its own copies of large arrays.

tags.why: Large speed-up for many k-points; costs memory.
tags.breaks: A value that does not divide the core count wastes cores; more groups use more memory.

corrections.was: KPAR must be a divisor of the total number of k-points.
corrections.now: That is not required; uneven division only causes load imbalance. The hard requirement is that the number of MPI ranks is divisible by KPAR.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: LWAVE
tags.default: .TRUE.

tags.why: Saves disk; SCF must write CHGCAR for later ICHARG=11 runs.

tags.name: LCHARG

tags.name: LDAU

tags.name: LDAUU

tags.name: LDAUJ

summary.intermediate: Per species: l channel (−1 none, 2 d, 3 f), U, J

tags.name: HFSCREEN

tags.name: AEXX

tags.name: ISYM
tags.default: 2 (PAW); 3 with hybrids
tags.typical: default; ISYM = 0 to switch off; SYMPREC 1E-4–1E-3

summary.beginner: Controls whether VASP uses crystal symmetry to save work. 0 switches it off.
summary.pro: 2: full symmetry; k-points reduced to the IBZ, densities symmetrized. 0: no space-group symmetry, but time reversal is still used (k and −k equivalent). −1: no symmetry at all, including time reversal; full k-mesh.

tags.why: Change only to fix symmetry errors or for LOBSTER/defects.
tags.breaks: Leaving it on can fight a hand-built antiferromagnetic MAGMOM pattern; changing it is only for fixing symmetry errors.

corrections.was: ISYM = −1: no k-point reduction, but symmetry still used elsewhere.
corrections.now: ISYM = −1 switches off all symmetry, including time reversal. ISYM = 0 is the setting that drops space-group symmetry but keeps time reversal.

tags.notes: Minimum VASP version is not stated in the handbooks and has not been checked.

tags.name: SYMPREC
